title: Buckhurst Hill & Loughton
intro: Two towns on the eastern edge of Epping Forest, with ancient hornbeams, Iron Age earthworks and Tudor history within a short walk or drive.

items.name: Connaught Water
items.blurb: A lake in Epping Forest with an easy path all the way round, near Chingford Plain.
items.tip: Arrive early at weekends: the car park fills up.

items.name: Queen Elizabeth's Hunting Lodge
items.blurb: A timber-framed hunting grandstand built for Henry VIII in 1543, free to visit, at the edge of the forest above Chingford Plain.
items.tip: The View visitor centre next door explains the forest.

items.name: Loughton Camp
items.blurb: The earth banks of an Iron Age hill fort hidden among old beech trees in the forest above Loughton.
items.tip: Easier to find with a map: it is deep in the trees.

items.name: Epping Forest beech woods
items.blurb: Old pollarded beech and hornbeam woods running north from Buckhurst Hill and Loughton, part of the City of London's great forest.
items.tip: Autumn colour peaks in late October.

items.name: Roding Valley Meadows
items.blurb: Wildflower meadows and hedgerows along the River Roding between Buckhurst Hill and Loughton, a Local Nature Reserve.
items.tip: Best in early summer when the meadows flower.
